In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of the carcinogenic compounds in cigarette smoke.
the identification and quantitation of the carcinogenic and tumorigenic components of cigarette smoke and their role in the induction of cancer in man.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PAH are not the sole or primary tumorigenic agents in cigarette smoke condensates.
the PAH are not the only carcinogenic components of cigarette smoke, but that they are an important component of the carcinogenic mixture in cigarette smoke.
the tumorigenic activity of CSC is due to the presence of a complex mixture of PAH, which must interact with other unidentified substances in order to exert their carcinogenic effects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the tumorigenic activity of cigarette smoke resides in the neutral fraction, which is composed of PAH, unidentified compounds, and other materials that are probably derived from the PAH.
the tumorigenicity of cigarette smoke condensation is not due to any single component, but is the result of an interaction between many components.
the PAH are present in cigarette smoke in a form that makes them inactive.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the carcinogenicity of cigarette smoke condense is due to the presence of polynuclear hydrocarbons and their synergistic interaction with other compounds in smoke.
the carcinogens in cigarette smoke are not just the known polynuclear aromatic compounds but rather the whole mixture, which contains hundreds of chemicals.
the PAH are important but not the only carcinogens in cigarette smoke.
